fields.reasoning: conduct is 690 and workflows 883 of the 1000-token TopicCap, so neither can hold the material; the facts live in internal/workflow/spec.go, internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml, internal/run/brief.go, internal/api/run_spawn.go and internal/api/workflow_new.go, and a test over those tables keeps the guide from drifting from them.
fields.statement: What a conductor looked up in Rhiza's code goes into three new guide topics, conduct-roles (spawn roles and check roles), conduct-handback (hand-back routes) and workflow-keys (every workflow key, step kind and default, and what rhiza workflow new writes), each named in the conduct topic's Read first and each pinned to the code by a guide test that iterates the code's own tables, so a key, role, declared check or route added to the code without the guide fails the test; the conduct and workflows topics are not grown past TopicCap to hold them.
fields.wording: Three new tested topics the conduct topic points to (derived from TopicCap and the code, autonomous plan run)

fields.reasoning: Routes and their order come from internal/workflow/builtin/ship-change.toml's on.* targets and comments, its conduct handback template (spawn the role, never fix it yourself), the handback.md shape in internal/run/brief.go, and the gate-fix, ci-fix and conflict-fix topics' own scopes; rhiza check and signoff have no dedicated fixer role, so the generic fixer takes them, as the fixer topic fixes findings given in its prompt.
fields.statement: A conductor handed back by ship-change reads handback.md (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands with their kept output, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files) and spawns, never fixes: gate's rhiza run build-check a verifier for the leaf lacking independent Evidence (a builder retry if it fails); gate's rhiza run review-check a critic for the check with an open blocker or major, then a fixer for confirmed findings and the checks again; gate's rhiza check a fixer with the output as its findings; gate's rhiza ship gate and the push step's rhiza ship open-pr (its pre-push check) the gate-fix role; signoff changes a fixer with the owner's requested changes, then the checks; wait-ci's timeout or merge's settled red CI the ci-fix role; merge's conflicting PR or moved main rhiza ship rebase --no-push (never plain ship rebase), then the conflict-fix role for a code conflict it leaves; every route lands and renders again, then rhiza session done. After handback_cap hand-backs (3 unless set) the next red parks the run stopped with an inbox item, and the steps after the merge never hand back.
fields.wording: Hand-back routes as ship-change and the fixer role topics give them (derived from the code, autonomous plan run)

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/guide -run 'TestConductRoles|TestConduct|TestList' shows the conduct-roles topic listed and under TopicCap, the conduct topic's Read first naming rhiza guide conduct-roles and staying under TopicCap, and conduct-roles naming each of the ten roles as rhiza guide <role> with every one a topic Lookup finds, plus --brief, --leaf, --check, --model, RHIZA_CHECK, RHIZA_CYCLE, [[step.<name>.check]], the arbiter and the refusal of an undeclared --check; the test parses the built-in ship-change with the workflow package and requires check-<name> for every check its conduct step declares; (failure case) the test fails naming the role when the topic lists a role with no guide topic of that name, or a check ship-change declares has no check-<name> line; go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run TestRunSpawnCheck still passes (an undeclared --check refused naming plan, code, qa); go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/guide passes.

fields.must_not: Change rhiza run spawn, the workflow package or any built-in workflow: guide text and its tests only; grow the conduct topic past TopicCap; change what the review index topic says
fields.statement: The guide has a conduct-roles topic, named in the conduct topic's Read first, listing every role a conductor spawns with rhiza run spawn (builder, verifier, check-plan, check-code, check-qa, critic, fixer, gate-fix, ci-fix, conflict-fix), each with the rhiza guide topic and skill it follows (its own name), when the conductor spawns it and the flags it takes (--brief always, --leaf for builder and verifier, --check <check> for a critic, --model optional), and the check roles: an agent step that declares [[step.<name>.check]] tables is a conductor step whose session and children put questions to the arbiter; a check-<check> role sets the child's RHIZA_CHECK and RHIZA_CYCLE; --check naming a check the step does not declare is refused with the declared names; the conductor default ship-change declares plan, code and qa, while compliance, quality and model belong to the classic workflows.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/guide -run 'TestConductHandback|TestConduct|TestList' shows the conduct-handback topic listed and under TopicCap, the conduct topic's Read first naming rhiza guide conduct-handback and staying under TopicCap, and conduct-handback naming handback.md's section titles as internal/run/brief.go renders them (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files), rhiza run build-check, rhiza run review-check, rhiza check, rhiza ship gate, rhiza ship open-pr, rhiza ship rebase --no-push, the roles verifier, critic, fixer, gate-fix, ci-fix and conflict-fix, handback_cap and rhiza session done; the test parses the built-in ship-change with the workflow package and requires the topic to name every step whose on.* target is handback:conduct and every command of its gate step; (failure case) the test fails naming the step or command when ship-change hands back from a step, or its gate runs a command, the topic does not name, and a step after the merge (main-ci, close-out, ship, deploy-check) named as handing back fails it; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/guide passes.

fields.must_not: Change the hand-back mechanism, handback.md's rendering, ship-change.toml or any fixer role topic: guide text and its tests only; grow the conduct topic past TopicCap; tell the conductor to fix anything itself
fields.statement: The guide has a conduct-handback topic, named in the conduct topic's Read first, giving the shape of handback.md (Failing step, Outcome, Failing commands with output paths, Output tail, Cause, Failed CI runs, Conflicted files) and, for each step of the conductor default ship-change that hands back to conduct, the route a conductor takes as conduct-handback-routes decides: the gate's four commands, signoff changes, push, wait-ci's timeout and merge (CI red, conflicting PR, moved main via rhiza ship rebase --no-push), each by spawning the named role, then land, render and rhiza session done; plus handback_cap and that the steps after the merge never hand back.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath ./internal/guide -run 'TestWorkflowKeys|TestWorkflowsText|TestConduct|TestList' shows the workflow-keys topic listed and under TopicCap; the test iterates workflow.FileKeys, workflow.SharedKeys, workflow.RoleKeys() and workflow.KindDocs() (each kind, its keys, tables and outcomes) and requires the topic to name each; it requires the defaults above, [[step.<name>.check]], rhiza workflow new with --from, handback:build, max_visits = 3 and the refusal of an existing file; TestWorkflowsText requires the workflows topic to name the gate kind and rhiza guide workflow-keys and the conduct topic's Read first names rhiza guide workflow-keys, both under TopicCap; (failure case) the test fails naming the key or kind when spec.go documents one the topic does not name; go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run TestScripts/guide passes.

fields.statement: The guide has a workflow-keys topic, named in the conduct topic's Read first and in the workflows topic, listing every top-level file key, shared step key, step kind (gate included) with its keys, sub-tables and outcomes, and role sub-table key that internal/workflow/spec.go documents, with the default each takes when unset (name the file's base name, start the first step, handback_cap 3, max_visits once, stall the watchdog's default, agent and permission_mode the run's, models the agent's default with the last kept, interval 10s or 30s with until, until_when idle, split auto, an autonomy stage rhiza.autonomy.<stage>, a cleanup name cleanup-<n>, a built-in arbiter when none is declared), that an agent step declaring [[step.<name>.check]] is a conductor step, and what rhiza workflow new writes: with --from a copy of the resolved workflow with its name set, without it a skeleton starting at an agent step build whose command step test is a placeholder that fails on purpose, with max_visits 3 and on.fail handback:build; it refuses an existing file and validates as workflow check does. The workflows topic's step kinds list names gate.
